behaviour.text: Kajan äter främst små ryggradslösa djur upp till 18 mm.
Den äter också säd, ogräsfrö, fläderbär, ekollon och odlade frukter, och söker föda främst på öppna markytor.

lead.text: The Western Jackdaw is a member of the crow family with black plumage, a grey nape and a strikingly pale iris.
It is often found near human settlements, and in winter larger flocks often gather in towns and cities.

fieldMarks.text: Black plumage with a grey nape, blue-black crown and dark grey underparts
Strikingly pale iris and a short, stout black bill
Male and female look alike, young birds have a brown iris and browner wings
Jerky wingbeats in flight and an upright stance on the ground

voice.text: Jackdaws are very talkative, especially in flocks, and can move around noisily.
Against predators it gives a hoarse, drawn-out "arrrrr" or "kaaaarr" alarm call.

whereWhen.text: The Western Jackdaw is a partial migrant that breeds in Sweden.
It occurs in southern and central Sweden and along the Norrland coast to Norrbotten, locally also in inland Norrland.
Some birds winter in Sweden, while others move south and return as early as March to April.
The Swedish population was estimated at 199 000 pairs in 2018.
It is reported all year round and from all 21 counties.

behaviour.text: It mainly eats small invertebrates up to 18 mm.
It also eats grain, weed seeds, elderberries, acorns and cultivated fruit, and feeds mainly on open ground.
Towards autumn jackdaws gather in flocks, often together with rooks and crows.
They usually breed in colonies, in cavities such as woodpecker holes or chimneys.
Almost all pairs that have been together for more than six months stay together for life.

text.text: At a distance the Western Jackdaw can be confused with a Rook, but the jackdaw is smaller, with a short bill and a grey nape.
